newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks rebound as optimism resurfaces.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks rebound as optimism resurfaces.

text.p: Austrian shares ended with solid gains on Wednesday, eked out on the back of firm international markets and growing optimism the blue-chip index has finally broken free of its tight trading range.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips advanced 15.6 points, or 1.48 percent, to 1,069.13 -- its highest close since July 11. Of its constituents, 19 gained, one fell and one was steady.
The ATX initially climbed as far as 1,073.11, driven by demand for market heavyweights like EA Generali and Creditanstalt.
One trader said that such buying indicated that "investors, even market makers, also joined in through the futures market."
Another trader attributed today's climb to short-covering.
"1,100 should be within sight," said the trader, adding that 1,050 is "very well supported, I doubt we'll be going below it."
The day's best performer was EA Generali, adding on 3.45 percent to 3,150, while the only decliner was Bank Austria's preferred shares, shedding 0.24 percent to 423.
Buying kicked off in the two Creditanstalt issues and then fanned out across the board, traders said.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index advanced 1.15 percent to 412.73.
The October ATX future gained 14 points to 1,069 on turnover of 1,157 contracts.
